title: Wastewater pathogen and vector attraction reduction practice questions
description: Free practice questions on sewage sludge pathogen and vector attraction reduction, 40 CFR 503 Subpart D. Every answer is explained and linked.

questions.question: Which example does the 503.31(d) definition give of land with a high potential for public exposure?

options.A: Agricultural land
options.B: Forest
options.C: A reclamation site located in a populated area
options.D: A reclamation site located in an unpopulated area

questions.explanation: Land with a high potential for public exposure "includes, but is not limited to, a public contact site and a reclamation site located in a populated area". Agricultural land, forest and a reclamation site in an unpopulated area are the examples of land with a low potential for public exposure.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 503.31, Special definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: This includes, but is not limited to, a public contact site and a reclamation site located in a populated area

questions.question: How does 503.31(k) define vector attraction?

options.A: The characteristic of sewage sludge that attracts rodents, flies, mosquitos, or other organisms capable of transporting infectious agents
options.B: The number of microorganisms per unit mass of total solids (dry weight) in the sewage sludge
options.C: The mass of oxygen consumed per unit time per unit mass of total solids in the sewage sludge
options.D: The disease-causing organisms in sewage sludge

questions.explanation: "Vector attraction is the characteristic of sewage sludge that attracts rodents, flies, mosquitos, or other organisms capable of transporting infectious agents." The other options describe density of microorganisms, specific oxygen uptake rate and pathogenic organisms.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 503.31, Special definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Vector attraction is the characteristic of sewage sludge that attracts rodents, flies, mosquitos, or other organisms capable of transporting infectious agents.

questions.topic: Class A: general rule and Alternatives 1 and 2
questions.question: Under 503.32(a)(1), what must a sewage sludge meet to be classified Class A with respect to pathogens?

options.A: All six alternatives in 503.32(a)(3) through (a)(8)
options.B: Any two of the alternatives in 503.32(a)(3) through (a)(8)
options.C: Only Alternative 1 in 503.32(a)(3)
options.D: The requirement in 503.32(a)(2) and one of the alternatives in 503.32(a)(3) through (a)(8)

questions.explanation: "The requirement in § 503.32(a)(2) and the requirements in either § 503.32(a)(3), (a)(4), (a)(5), (a)(6), (a)(7), or (a)(8) shall be met for a sewage sludge to be classified Class A with respect to pathogens."
questions.evidence: The requirement in § 503.32(a)(2) and the requirements in either § 503.32(a)(3), (a)(4), (a)(5), (a)(6), (a)(7), or (a)(8) shall be met for a sewage sludge to be classified Class A with respect to pathogens.

questions.topic: Class A: general rule and Alternatives 1 and 2
questions.question: 503.32(a)(2) says the Class A pathogen requirements must be met either before or at the same time as the vector attraction reduction requirements. Which vector attraction reduction requirements does it except from that order?
questions.explanation: The Class A requirements "shall be met either prior to meeting or at the same time the vector attraction reduction requirements in § 503.33, except the vector attraction reduction requirements in § 503.33 (b)(6) through (b)(8), are met."
questions.evidence: except the vector attraction reduction requirements in § 503.33 (b)(6) through (b)(8), are met

questions.topic: Class A: general rule and Alternatives 1 and 2
questions.question: In the Class A density requirement, what is the alternative to the fecal coliform density?

options.A: An enteric virus density of less than one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids
options.B: A Salmonella sp. bacteria density of less than three Most Probable Number per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis)
options.C: A geometric mean fecal coliform density from seven samples
options.D: A viable helminth ova density of less than one per four grams of total solids

questions.explanation: Alternative 1 reads: "Either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge shall be less than 1000 Most Probable Number per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of Salmonella sp. bacteria in the sewage sludge shall be less than three Most Probable Number per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis)". Enteric viruses and helminth ova are separate steps in Alternatives 3 and 4, and the seven-sample geometric mean is Class B Alternative 1.
questions.evidence: or the density of Salmonella sp. bacteria in the sewage sludge shall be less than three Most Probable Number per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis)

questions.topic: Class A: general rule and Alternatives 1 and 2
questions.question: Under Class A Alternative 1, what time period does 503.32(a)(3)(ii)(B) set when the sludge is seven percent solids or higher and small particles of sludge are heated by warmed gases or an immiscible liquid?

options.A: 20 minutes or longer
options.B: 30 minutes or longer
options.C: 72 hours
options.D: 15 seconds or longer

questions.explanation: In that case "the temperature of the sewage sludge shall be 50 degrees Celsius or higher; the time period shall be 15 seconds or longer; and the temperature and time period shall be determined using equation (2)." The 20-minute period in (A) applies "except when small particles of sewage sludge are heated by either warmed gases or an immiscible liquid."
questions.evidence: the temperature of the sewage sludge shall be 50 degrees Celsius or higher; the time period shall be 15 seconds or longer; and the temperature and time period shall be determined using equation (2).

questions.question: Under Class A Alternative 3, when the enteric virus density before pathogen treatment is less than one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids, how long is the sludge Class A with respect to enteric viruses?

options.A: Until the next monitoring episode for the sewage sludge
options.B: For one year
options.C: For 30 days
options.D: Until the end of the 72 hour period

questions.explanation: In that case "the sewage sludge is Class A with respect to enteric viruses until the next monitoring episode for the sewage sludge."
questions.evidence: the sewage sludge is Class A with respect to enteric viruses until the next monitoring episode for the sewage sludge.

questions.question: Class A Alternative 3 has the sludge analyzed for enteric viruses before pathogen treatment. Under Alternative 4 (503.32(a)(6)(ii)), which of these is one of the times the enteric virus density must be less than one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids?

options.A: Only before pathogen treatment
options.B: Within eight hours after discharge from the pathogen treatment process
options.C: At the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed
options.D: At the end of the 72 hour period of high pH

questions.explanation: "The density of enteric viruses in the sewage sludge shall be less than one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed"; the rule also lists other times.
questions.evidence: The density of enteric viruses in the sewage sludge shall be less than one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed

questions.question: Under Class A Alternative 6, who determines that a process is equivalent to a Process to Further Reduce Pathogens?

options.A: The permitting authority
options.B: The person who prepares the sewage sludge
options.C: The person who applies the sewage sludge
options.D: The owner of the land where the sludge is applied

questions.explanation: The sludge "shall be treated in a process that is equivalent to a Process to Further Reduce Pathogens, as determined by the permitting authority."
questions.evidence: shall be treated in a process that is equivalent to a Process to Further Reduce Pathogens, as determined by the permitting authority.

questions.topic: Class B pathogen requirements and site restrictions
questions.question: Under Class B Alternative 1, which value of the fecal coliform densities in the seven samples is compared with the limit?

options.A: The arithmetic mean
options.B: The highest single sample
options.C: The median
options.D: The geometric mean

questions.explanation: "The geometric mean of the density of fecal coliform in the samples collected in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section shall be less than" the stated values.
questions.evidence: The geometric mean of the density of fecal coliform in the samples collected in paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section shall be less than

questions.topic: Class B pathogen requirements and site restrictions
questions.question: For food crops with harvested parts below the land surface, what decides whether the 20-month or the 38-month harvest restriction in 503.32(b)(5) applies?

options.A: Whether the land has a high or low potential for public exposure
options.B: How long the sewage sludge remains on the land surface prior to incorporation into the soil
options.C: The percent solids of the sewage sludge
options.D: Which Class B alternative the sewage sludge met

questions.explanation: The 20-month restriction applies "when the sewage sludge remains on the land surface for four months or longer prior to incorporation into the soil" and the 38-month restriction "when the sewage sludge remains on the land surface for less than four months prior to incorporation into the soil."
questions.evidence: when the sewage sludge remains on the land surface for less than four months prior to incorporation into the soil.

questions.topic: Class B pathogen requirements and site restrictions
questions.question: When does the one-year turf harvest restriction in 503.32(b)(5)(vi) apply, unless otherwise specified by the permitting authority?

options.A: Whenever turf is grown on any land where sewage sludge is applied
options.B: Only when animals have grazed on the land
options.C: When the harvested turf is placed on either land with a high potential for public exposure or a lawn
options.D: Only when the sewage sludge was injected below the land surface

questions.explanation: Turf "shall not be harvested for one year after application of the sewage sludge when the harvested turf is placed on either land with a high potential for public exposure or a lawn, unless otherwise specified by the permitting authority."
questions.evidence: when the harvested turf is placed on either land with a high potential for public exposure or a lawn, unless otherwise specified by the permitting authority.

questions.question: Domestic septage applied to agricultural land, forest, or a reclamation site meets the pH option in 503.32(c)(2). Which site restrictions must still be met?

options.A: None; the pH treatment replaces the site restrictions
options.B: Only the grazing restriction in 503.32(b)(5)(v)
options.C: Only the public access restrictions in 503.32(b)(5)(vii) and (viii)
options.D: The site restrictions in 503.32(b)(5)(i) through (b)(5)(iv)

questions.explanation: The pH must be raised to 12 or higher and remain there for 30 minutes "and the site restrictions in § 503.32 (b)(5)(i) through (b)(5)(iv) shall be met."
questions.evidence: and the site restrictions in § 503.32 (b)(5)(i) through (b)(5)(iv) shall be met.

questions.question: What does vector attraction reduction option 503.33(b)(12) require?

options.A: The pH of domestic septage raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without more alkali, kept at 12 or higher for 30 minutes
options.B: The pH raised to 12 or higher and kept there for two hours, then at 11.5 or higher for an additional 22 hours
options.C: The pH raised to above 12 and kept above 12 for 72 hours
options.D: Enough lime added to raise the pH to 12 after two hours of contact

questions.explanation: "The pH of domestic septage shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali, shall remain at 12 or higher for 30 minutes." The other options describe 503.33(b)(6), Class A Alternative 2 and the lime stabilization PSRP.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 503.33, Vector attraction reduction (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The pH of domestic septage shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali, shall remain at 12 or higher for 30 minutes.

questions.topic: Where each vector attraction reduction option applies
questions.question: Which range of vector attraction reduction options does 503.33(a)(2) allow for bulk sewage sludge applied to a lawn or a home garden?

options.A: One of 503.33(b)(1) through (b)(10)
options.B: One of 503.33(b)(1) through (b)(11)
options.C: One of 503.33(b)(1) through (b)(8)

questions.explanation: "One of the vector attraction reduction requirements in § 503.33 (b)(1) through (b)(8) shall be met when bulk sewage sludge is applied to a lawn or a home garden."

questions.question: In the anaerobic bench-scale option in 503.33(b)(2), what result at the end of the 40 additional days shows that vector attraction reduction is achieved?

options.A: The volatile solids are reduced by less than 17 percent
options.B: The volatile solids are reduced by more than 17 percent
options.C: The volatile solids are reduced by less than 15 percent
options.D: The volatile solids are reduced by at least 38 percent

questions.explanation: "When at the end of the 40 days, the volatile solids in the sewage sludge at the beginning of that period is reduced by less than 17 percent, vector attraction reduction is achieved."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 503.33, Vector attraction reduction (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: When at the end of the 40 days, the volatile solids in the sewage sludge at the beginning of that period is reduced by less than 17 percent, vector attraction reduction is achieved.

questions.question: What decides whether the 75 percent solids option in 503.33(b)(7) or the 90 percent solids option in 503.33(b)(8) applies?

options.A: Whether the sludge is Class A or Class B
options.B: Whether the sludge was aerobically or anaerobically digested
options.C: Whether the sludge will be applied to a lawn or to agricultural land
options.D: Whether the sludge contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process

questions.explanation: (b)(7) covers sewage sludge "that does not contain unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process" and (b)(8) covers sewage sludge "that contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 503.33, Vector attraction reduction (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The percent solids of sewage sludge that contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 90 percent

questions.question: What does vector attraction reduction option 503.33(b)(11) require?

options.A: Incorporation into the soil within six hours after application
options.B: Covering sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit with soil or other material at the end of each operating day
options.C: Injection below the surface of the land
options.D: Treatment in an aerobic process for 14 days or longer

questions.explanation: "Sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit shall be covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day." Incorporation, injection and aerobic treatment are other options.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 503.33, Vector attraction reduction (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit shall be covered with soil or other material at the end of each operating day.

questions.question: Which of these processes does Appendix B list as a Process to Further Reduce Pathogens (PFRP)?

options.A: Air drying
options.B: Lime stabilization
options.C: Pasteurization
options.D: Anaerobic digestion

questions.explanation: Appendix B lists "Pasteurization—The temperature of the sewage sludge is maintained at 70 degrees Celsius or higher for 30 minutes or longer" under the Processes to Further Reduce Pathogens. Air drying, lime stabilization and anaerobic digestion are listed as Processes To Significantly Reduce Pathogens.
